Hi Naomi —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. To recap: our events engine spiked in May (attached usage_report_May2027.csv) and we're already seeing similar growth trends for June. We'd like to avoid unpredictable overage charges and make a clean plan for Q3.

Two asks from our side: 1) Can we increase our hosted commit from 6M tokens/mo to 10M tokens/mo starting Aug 1? 2) We want a mechanism to protect us from sudden surges — something like a temporary escrow of additional commit (billed pro-rata) or a soft-cap that gracefully throttles with clear burst credits.

If you can sketch commercial options and timelines, procurement will prep a PO/standard SOW. Happy to jump on a short call with billing/legal if helpful.

Cheers,
Rajiv
Head of Platform Engineering
Atlas Retail

Rajiv — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. I reviewed the usage file and shared with Ben/Karthik. High level response: we can support a jump to 10M tokens/mo for August with a short-term consumption escrow model plus a soft-cap/burst pocket that applies until the next billing cycle.

I'm attaching an initial SOW template for Atlas that captures: new commit level (10M tokens/mo), a 90-day soft-cap policy (grace burst equal to 30% of monthly commit billed at discounted overage rate), and an escrow option where Atlas prepays 50% of the uplift to lock capacity while we provision dedicated pool reservations.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben, can you confirm the discounted overage rate and whether the escrow triggers dedicated capacity reservations?
- Karthik, can you share the updated throughput/latency SLA expectations for the 10M baseline and the burst pocket?
- Rajiv/procurement, if you can confirm the procurement contact and PO timing we’ll produce a clean SOW for signature.

I’ll hold a 30-min slot Thurs 10am PT in case we need to iron out numbers.

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 usage + options for smoothing overages

Naomi / Rajiv — quick commercial note from the ops side. We can offer the 10M tokens/mo commit effective Aug 1. Proposed pricing: base commit price = $0.0018/token (monthly commit). For the soft-cap burst pocket (30% additional capacity), overage billing at a discounted rate = $0.0022/token (vs standard $0.0030).

Escrow note: if Atlas prepays 50% of the uplift ($0.0018 * 4M tokens * 50% for the partial month), we can prioritize a dedicated reservation window and guarantee reserved GPU slots for the first 60 days. If the prepaid escrow is used up, remaining usage falls to the soft-cap/overage cadence above.

Operational caveat: to guarantee the dedicated reservation we need a confirmed commit and PO by July 15 to align with capacity planning for Aug. If that date is tight we can do a temporary burst policy without dedicated reservations (still with discounted overage).

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success Ops | Redwood Inference

Ben/Naomi/Rajiv — technical confirmation from Platform Product: the 10M baseline is straightforward for our hosted runtime. Expected P95 latency impact is <5% for typical prompt distributions once we enable auto-batching with the new reservation window. Burst pocket (30%) will be served from the same pool but protected via priority routing; we will apply graceful degradation rules (latency-first) when sustained burst exceeds pocket.

For SLA language: we can commit to a 99.5% uptime for inference with an SLO for median latency uplift thresholds. We’ll add a clause that if monthly consumption exceeds 150% of committed tokens two months in a row, we’ll require a capacity re-evaluation and discuss an amended commit (to avoid repeated over-provisioning risk).

I’ll prepare a short appendix for the SOW that maps token bands to expected throughput and sample latency numbers (will send by Thu EOD).

—Karthik
